title: Polaris Therapeutics POC: unit economics & performance roadmap
summary: Discovery + POC scoping to define success metrics and a 6-week pilot for unit economics benchmarking. Customer needs a cost-limited pilot (target <$12k/mo equivalent) and a go/no-go based on 95th p99 latency for 256-token completions and end-to-end accuracy on 5 canonical prompts. Discussed batching, prefix cache, quantization tradeoffs and security requirements (VPC, SSO, KMS). Agreed next steps: Redwood to share cost model spreadsheet, pilot SOW draft, and run initial perf test with 10k sample queries.
next_steps: Redwood: Share pilot SOW + cost model spreadsheet (Maya) — due 2026-10-11
Customer: Provide 5 canonical prompt sets and 10k anonymized queries (Sunita) — due 2026-10-13
Schedule 1-hour benchmark run (SE + Customer) week of 2026-10-18
action_items: Maya Chen: Send pilot SOW and example benchmark harness + GCP/AWS region options (2026-10-11)
Liam O'Connor: Prepare initial per-token cost scenarios and latency targets, include quantization options (2026-10-12)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-10-07 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Rhea Patel (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (VP Eng, Polaris), Dr. Sunita Malhotra (ML Lead), Ethan Cole (CTO), Priya Rao (Security)

SUMMARY & GOALS (auto): quick alignment on success criteria, cost envelope, and pilot timeline.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intro then we'll jump to what success looks like for you. um Alex, do you want to kick off with the top-line ask?
[00:18] Alex: yeah thanks Maya. hi all. high level — we want to run a short pilot to understand per-token economics and whether Redwood's hosted/dedicated options can meet our latency targets under our budget. concretely, we run inference for clinical note summarization; typical completion 200-300 tokens, and peak concurrent users approx 120. budget target is roughly under twelve thousand dollars a month if possible.
[00:42] Dr. Sunita: and importantly we need fidelity on 5 clinical prompt templates — those are our quality gate. we can't accept hallucinations; so accuracy/ROUGE-ish metrics matter as a go/no-go.
[00:58] Liam: great, thanks. two quick clarifying q's: 1) are those 120 concurrent users sustained or bursts? 2) what cloud regions are you constrained to?
[01:16] Alex: mostly bursty, 1-2 minute spikes during clinician shift changes. average qps around 80, peaks around 450 for short windows. region: primarly us-east, but some EU data residency for a subset — we'll need options.
[01:36] Rhea: thanks — that's helpful. for cost modeling we'll model both hosted baseline and a dedicated pool with predictable throughput. rough ballpark on per-token: we'll show a hosted baseline and then a dedicated profile that drops unit cost 25-40% depending on batching and quantization.
[01:56] Ethan: are you able to do on-prem or VPC? data sensitivity means some notes must stay in our VPC.
[02:06] Maya: yes, Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem packaging. for the pilot we typically run a Private trial into your VPC or we can run dedicated in Redwoods controlled infra with strict retention controls. Priya, what are your must-haves from a security perspective?
[02:22] Priya: SOC2 is table stakes, we need SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs to our SIEM, and KMS integration for keys. for the pilot we need audit logs delivered and a signed DPA.
[02:38] Maya: sign — we'll include SOC2 cert and our security whitepaper. SSO + KMS are supported; we'll capture KMS details in the next steps.

Benchmarks & Workload sizing discussion:
[02:52] Liam: quick sketch for the bench: 10k sample queries across the 5 templates to validate quality; perf bench with 1,000 qps sustained for 60s bursts and 450 qps peak testing to emulate your spikes. target p95/p99 latency numbers for 256-token completions?
[03:14] Alex: p95 under 250ms, p99 under 600ms for our interactive flow — but we can flex if the accuracy tradeoff is higher.
[03:26] Liam: ok that's reasonable. note that p99 for 256 tokens is dominated by GPU scheduling + KV cache misses. we can use prefix/KV caching to reduce cold-start latency for repeated templates; that can give you a 30-50% reduction on repeated flows.
[03:47] Dr. Sunita: what's the expected per-token cost here? we need estimates to compare against our current deployed API (about $0.0015/token effective with heavy batching).
[03:58] Rhea: initial quick numbers: hosted baseline with a transformer ~ 0.0009-0.0011 per token (no quantization, moderate batching). Dedicated with optimized batching and int8 quantization path could be ~0.00045-0.0007 per token. these are rough; we'll run the pilot bench to instrument.
[04:20] Alex: ok that would be a 1.5-3x improvement — good. but what drives variance?
[04:27] Liam: main levers are 1) batch size (larger batch = higher throughput efficiency but increased latency), 2) KV/prefix caching (saves compute on repeated context), 3) quantization (small quality drop, big cost win), and 4) routing policies (cross-region vs local). we'll include scenario tables in the cost sheet.
[04:48] Ethan: how do you handle fallbacks if you lose capacity in a region? we can't have clinicians down.
[04:55] Maya: smart routing + fallback: we can route to a compatible model variant in another region or to a smaller/cheaper model as a graceful degradation; you'll configure failover policies in the rollout.

On accuracy & evals:
[05:08] Dr. Sunita: for our domain, small token-level changes matter; we'll need a labeled eval set. we'll provide expected outputs for the 5 canonical prompts. will you run automated regression alerts during the pilot?
[05:22] Liam: yes, Redwood Optimize can run prompt-set based regression alerts; for pilot we'll set thresholds and alert on quality drop > 3% relative F1/ROUGE.
[05:34] Rhea: also we'll capture token-level cost per route and per model in the console so you can see cost breakdown by template.

Cost modeling specifics (numbers, scenarios):
[05:44] Liam: sample scenario A: hosted small GPU, no quantization, batching 8 avg, expected p95 ~180ms, per-token ~0.0010. Scenario B: dedicated reserved pool, int8 quant, batching 16 avg, prefix cache hit 40%, p95 ~160ms, per-token ~0.00055. Scenario C: emergency fallback to smaller 7B variant for 10% of requests, reduces per-token to ~0.00035 but loses ~4-6% accuracy on complex prompts.
[06:14] Alex: can you model the monthly cost for our workload? 100k tokens/day average, peaks as described, 30 days.
[06:22] Rhea: rough calc: 100k tokens/day -> 3M tokens/month. Scenario B per-token 0.00055 -> $1,650/month compute; add overhead for networking, storage, and reserved capacity amortization -> we'd model it in the cost sheet to land near your $10-12k target depending on commitment and retention windows. we'll put a sensitivity table.
[06:46] Priya: retention windows — what logs do you retain by default? we need short retention for PHI.
[06:54] Maya: by default hosted retains logs for X days, but Private/VPC you control retention. for PHI we'll recommend VPC + no retention or customer-managed KMS to ensure keys are in your control. we'll document that in the SOW.

Pilot timeline and success criteria:
[07:10] Maya: proposed 6-week plan: week 0-1: exec kickoff + security onboarding; week 2: run quality evals on 10k query set; week 3: perf benchmarking (peak simulation); week 4-5: tuning (batching, quant, cache), week 6: deliver final econ report + go/no-go recommendation. Success criteria: 1) accuracy threshold on canonical prompts (>= target metric Sunita provides), 2) p95/p99 latency within agreed ranges or documented tradeoffs, 3) predicted unit cost under your budget envelope.
[07:40] Dr. Sunita: sounds fair. will there be an SLO for inference latency in the pilot?
[07:46] Liam: we'll instrument p50/p95/p99 and provide raw traces; SLOs are advisory for the pilot — production SLOs can be SLA-backed when you're on Dedicated with a commitment.

Security/legal touchpoints:
[07:58] Priya: we'll need DPA, SOC2, and a network diagram. also KMS details for key rotation policy. can Redwood do HSM integration?
[08:10] Maya: yes for Private we support customer-managed keys and HSM/KMS integrations. we'll attach the security pack.

Edge cases & technical deep-dive snippets:
[08:22] Liam: on the perf side a few notes – continuous batching in our runtime means short requests can piggyback into batches, but long context lengths reduce batching efficiency. also KV cache is per-model-instance so warm-up for repeated templates is fast. quantization: int8 gives ~20-40% perf lift but watch for a small quality delta on rare tokens; we'll run AB tests.
[08:52] Alex: would you recommend dedicated immediately or start hosted?
[08:56] Rhea: recommended path: pilot on Dedicated trial for predictable latency and better unit economics; if you want faster time-to-value we can start hosted but that likely costs more per token. we can include both in scenario analysis.

Wrap & next steps recap:
[09:08] Maya: recap — Redwood will: 1) send pilot SOW + security pack + cost model spreadsheet, 2) schedule benchmark run w/ SE + customer (week of 10/18), 3) provide region options and dedicated sizing recommendations. Polaris will: provide canonical prompts and 10k queries, share security questionnaire and confirm internal stakeholders for pilot sign-off.
[09:36] Alex: thanks. one ask — can you include a short table in the cost sheet that maps accuracy degradation to cost savings so leadership can see tradeoffs quickly?
[09:46] Liam: absolutely, we'll include a quality vs cost sensitivity table and a recommended default config.
[09:52] Dr. Sunita: also include how we might handle model rollouts and canarying for new versions — we need to track regressions over time.
[09:59] Rhea: Redwood Optimize supports canarying and prompt-set regression alerts, we'll include runbook steps.

Closing notes (imperfect transcriptions / minor overlaps):
[10:12] Maya: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the doc set.
[10:16] Ethan: thanks all, look forward to the SOW.
[10:19] [end]
